newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Free State premier Patrick Lekota, his entire cabinet and the ANC provincial executive would be removed from office, the party's national leadership said in Johannesburg on Monday.

- Deputy President Thabo Mbeki is to lead a high-powered delegation on an eight-nation visit to Europe to lobby influential capitals for better market access before formal trade talks start later this month.
- The State Tender Board should be scrapped and its functions devolved to departments, a draft green paper on procurement policy has proposed.

- Efforts to have a 10,000-strong South African National Defence Force (SANDF) ready for peacekeeping duties in central Africa were being accelerated and it was expected that the "lakes states" would help determine South Africa's role in the troubled region, Deputy Defence minister Ronnie Kasrils said on Monday.
- Ostrich co-operative Klein Karoo Kooperasie has shut two Oudtshoorn abattoirs following a suspected outbreak of Congo fever linked to abattoir workers who were exposed to ostrich meat.

- British Airways has warned it will cut its four weekly flights to Cape Town unless it is granted extra flights to South Africa to compete with Virgin Atlantic's plans to expand its new South African business.

- Visa International has entered into a partnership with First National Bank and Nedcor Bank to offer smart cards, or banking cards with built-in microchips, which can significantly increase the kinds of transactions clients can do with one bank card, the company said on Monday.

- Three of the seven foreign telecommunications companies which the government said less than a month ago were queuing to buy a stake in Telkom next year have dropped out of the race, Jay Naidoo, the posts and telecommunicatiuons minister announced on Monday.

- Forbes, the financial and professional services group, staged a spectacular debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday. Following a placing of 60 million rand worth of shares at 5.35 rand per share, Forbes opened at seven rand per share and then raced up to 8.15 rand before closing at eight rand.

- The African National Congress (ANC) on Monday took one of the most far-reaching decisions yet in its two-and-a-half years of governance, by firing Free State premier Patrick "Terror" Lekota, his entire cabinet and the entire provincial executive of the organisation.
- A woman has died and seven others are being treated in hospital for suspected Congo fever after a mystery disease hit workers at an ostrich abattoir near Oudtshoorn.

- The government was "extremely displeased" with the refusal of apartheid-era military generals to provide specific information on past deeds to the Truth and Reconciliation Committee, Deputy Defence Minister Ronnie Kasrils said on Monday.

- A Cape-Town-based man who describes himself as a "commodities dealer" claims to have sold a stock of deadly landmines to South Africans who planned to put them in their gardens near high security walls.
